html:
A comic novel by Miguel de Cervantes, published in two parts in 1605 and 1615. It is often called the first modern novel.

A country gentleman from La Mancha in Spain reads so many tales of knights that he loses his grip on reality. He renames himself Don Quixote, puts on old armour and rides out to right wrongs, with a plain farmer, Sancho Panza, as his squire. He attacks windmills he takes for giants and treats inns as castles.

The book began as a parody, but it became much more. The two men talk and change each other over the journey, and the reader sees one world through two very different minds. In the second part the characters even know that a book about them has been published. Cervantes wrote that part partly in answer to a fake sequel by another author.

It was a hit at once and was soon translated into English and French. It shaped later novelists from Fielding and Dickens to Dostoevsky, and the word "quixotic" comes from it.
